entrypoints.summary: Unauthenticated registration POST to /ajax/api/user/save with securitytoken=guest can supply user[searchprefs].

affected_components.file: vB_DataManager_User validfields definition and verify_serialized validator (embedded writeup excerpts)
affected_components.role: Marks searchprefs TYPE_NOCLEAN and calls unserialize during validation.
Maps unknown class names to project paths and requires an existing computed PHP file.

causal_paths.kind: HTTP registration input to unsafe deserialization

negative_controls: No bundled execution result demonstrates the full chain on an affected target.
No bundled execution result demonstrates rejection or harmless handling on a fixed target.
observability.positive_marker: The source reports pre-authentication remote code execution; no independent runtime output or command-result artifact is bundled.

preconditions: A vBulletin version within the writeup's reported affected scope is deployed.
The registration endpoint is reachable to an unauthenticated guest.
The described package layout and autoloader behavior are present; the writeup reports Monolog under packages/googlelogin/vendor/monolog.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Form-encoded POST to /ajax/api/user/save with securitytoken=guest and user[searchprefs] containing PHP serialized object data.
trigger_steps.summary: Send the documented guest registration POST with a serialized value in user[searchprefs].

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Serialized object graph combining an autoload-triggering class name with a Monolog RCE1 destructor-vector object graph.
trigger_steps.summary: Use an unknown serialized class name to invoke vBulletin's autoloader and, as described by the writeup, include the disabled package's vendor autoloader before supplying a Monolog gadget chain.

relation_candidates.rationale: The reported guest registration request supplies user[searchprefs], whose validator calls unserialize on non-array submitted input.
The writeup explains that deserializing an unknown class invokes registered autoloaders and that vBulletin's autoloader computes and requires a project path from the class name.
The writeup reports loading the disabled package's vendor autoloader to make Monolog classes available, while the PHPGGC artifact defines a Monolog RCE1 chain with __destruct as its vector.
The research post characterizes the chain as pre-authentication remote code execution, and the gadget artifact is explicitly an RCE function-call chain.
The writeup reports that the issue was patched in 5.6.9 PL1, 5.6.8 PL1, and 5.6.7 PL1; exact patch semantics are not bundled.

impact.affected_asset: vBulletin application process and its code-execution privileges.
impact.attacker_capability: A remote unauthenticated requester can submit serialized object data that reaches deserialization and, as reported, activate an autoload-assisted Monolog destructor gadget chain.

causal_trace.summary: A guest registration request supplies a serialized value through the optional, TYPE_NOCLEAN user searchprefs field.

The field's verify_serialized validator invokes unserialize on non-array, nonempty submitted data in order to validate it, so untrusted serialized objects are processed during pre-authentication registration.

PHP deserialization may invoke vBulletin's registered autoloader; the documented class-name-to-lowercase underscore-path mapping can require an existing project PHP file. The writeup describes using this behavior to load the otherwise-disabled googlelogin vendor autoloader and make Monolog classes available.

With Monolog classes made available, the reported PHPGGC Monolog RCE1 destructor-vector chain constructs SyslogUdpHandler and BufferHandler objects using attacker-selected function and parameter values; the writeup characterizes the overall condition as pre-authentication remote code execution.

failure.operation: PHP unserialize() invoked by verify_serialized(&$data) on attacker-controlled user[searchprefs]

primary_invariant.statement: Registration-time validation of searchprefs must not deserialize attacker-controlled data in a way that processes arbitrary object classes, autoload side effects, or object lifecycle behavior.
primary_invariant.violated_because: verify_serialized calls unserialize on a submitted non-array value before reserializing it, and the submitted searchprefs field is reachable by a guest registration request.

quality.review_notes: Primary evidence is a public research writeup with embedded code and a concrete request, plus a version-pinned PHPGGC gadget definition. No controlled run result is bundled, and no accessible vendor patch/diff confirms exact remediation semantics or independently verifies final command execution.

remediation.invariant_restored: The writeup reports fixed patch-level releases, but the bundle contains no vendor patch or diff establishing the exact code-level invariant-restoring change.
mitigation_classes: upgrade to a reported vendor security-patch release
prevent untrusted registration input from undergoing object deserialization during serialized-field validation

target.component: User registration ORM validation for vB_DataManager_User searchprefs

oracle.expected_negative: On a reported fixed patch-level release, the same untrusted serialized-object submission should no longer yield attacker-controlled object-deserialization behavior. No bundled execution result establishes this outcome.
oracle.expected_positive: On a reported affected installation, submit the documented guest request to /ajax/api/user/save with a serialized user[searchprefs] value and observe that the registration validation path reaches its deserialization handling; the writeup supplies such a PoC request.
